long_biography.plain_text:
Milk quotas changed the course of William McNamara’s career. After agricultural college, he had taken over one of his father’s Pembrokeshire farms and built a 400-cow dairy herd. When production limits arrived in 1984, he moved the cattle and devoted part of the land to a new family attraction. Oakwood grew from BMX bikes and go-karts into a leading British theme park.

Oakwood’s outdoor model depended on summer weather and visitors already staying nearby. McNamara left the park to pursue an all-weather destination that could draw guests throughout the year, spent years securing planning approval and opened Bluestone in 2008. The family-controlled resort launched with lodges, a water park and indoor leisure facilities, survived the financial crisis and developed an employee shareholding alongside its environmental and community commitments.
